decisions.decision: Treat the following as already closed and do not re-implement them: enrollment challenge/replay/single-use (TestEnrollmentChallengeSignatureAndReplay, TestEnrollmentRejectsTamperedChallenge, TestEnrollmentTokenIsConsumedOnFirstBegin), the HTTP enrollment leg (internal/api TestRunnerEnrollmentHTTPChallengeFlow), journal fsync/idempotency/partial-tail recovery/corruption rejection (TestJournalRecoveryAndIdempotentAppend, TestJournalRejectsCorruptCompleteLine), workspace path/symlink/permission validation and the argv/env secret guards (TestWorkspaceAndGuard), control receipt/observation journaling (TestControlLoopFsyncsReceiptAndObservation, TestControlLoopImmediateStopUnknownObservation), the in-process single-Execution fake journey with request-id idempotent retry (TestOrchestratorFakeJourney), provider argv/stdin/parse/usage-suppression and secret-fixture rejection (internal/provider TestAdaptersBuildSafeArgvAndParseMetadata, TestFixturesRejectSecretsAndMalformed, TestFailureClassificationAndHandoff), canonical expired-lease reclaim with a fence bump (internal/application TestExpiredLeaseCanBeReclaimed), canonical lost-execution fencing (internal/reconciler TestTickExpiresLeaseAndFencingLostExecution), and atomic binary update/rollback (internal/update TestInstallSwitchAndRollbackKeepBothVersions, TestVerifyRejectsTamperAndIncompatibleSchema). V2-016 adds only the gaps named in d4 through d12.
decisions.rationale: Measured, not assumed: devbox run --pure -- go test -v ./internal/runner reports exactly 11 passing tests and ./internal/provider exactly 3. Re-asserting covered behaviour spends Luna context and inflates the runner evidence without moving any M3 completion condition.

decisions.decision: Do not create test/journeys/ in V2-016. Journey tests live in internal/runner as new files (journey_test.go, crash_test.go), inside the existing runner component.
decisions.rationale: internal/ci/planner.go evidenceKey() unconditionally includes ci/components.json in every component hash (include := p == "ci/components.json" || go.mod || go.sum || devbox.lock), and ci/** is in all_on_change. Adding a component therefore invalidates the evidence key of all 23 components and every committed evidence record, including the M0 and M1 gate evidence, while two other implementers are concurrently editing .agents/v2/evidence/**. The cost is not optional either: ValidateTracked requires exactly one owning component per tracked file, so test/journeys/** cannot exist at all without the ci/components.json edit, and make ownership (part of make check) would fail. validation.md section 2 constrains journey shape (independent, own fixture, own timeout, no dependence on another journey's execution order or residual processes), not directory location; one top-level Go test function per journey, t.TempDir() fixtures, per-test context deadlines and zero package-level mutable state satisfy that shape exactly. The roadmap repository layout move to test/journeys/ is deferred to a milestone boundary where re-evidencing is already being paid, and is escalated as such.

decisions.decision: Journey scope for V2-016 is the local segment of validation.md journey 1 (issue intake to Increment Artifact) and journey 4 (Runner loss, fencing, resume in a different Execution). Both run fully in process against internal/application over internal/store/memory with an injected clock and injected id generator; no HTTP server, no real Provider CLI, no wall-clock sleep, no goroutine timer.
decisions.rationale: The journeys' subject is the Runner state machine, and the HTTP transport for the same routes already has contract coverage in internal/api (TestRouteContractErrorsAndRunnerPermitRole, TestRunnerEnrollmentHTTPChallengeFlow, TestStrictJSONAuthRoleAndSpoof). Repeating the journey over HTTP would duplicate transport coverage and place a runner-owned assertion in the api component's evidence. internal/api imports internal/runner, so a same-package test could not import it back without a cycle in any case. Enrollment stays in the chain without HTTP because runner.Service lives in the same package: the journey issues an enrollment, completes the challenge, verifies the session, and uses the resulting runner id as the claim caller identity.

decisions.decision: Verify crash resume in two layers with a clean split of what each layer proves. Layer A (deterministic, gate-bearing): an in-process journey that abandons Execution 1 after its durable journal write, advances the injected clock past LeaseTTL, re-claims the same Increment, and asserts a new Execution id, a strictly greater fencing token, resume from the recorded local checkpoint, and rejection of Execution 1's late AcceptResult. Layer B (real process, narrow): one test that re-executes the test binary as a child (os.Args[0] plus a helper env var), has the child open a real runner.Journal, append and fsync one event, write a marker file and block, then SIGKILLs the child's process group and asserts the fsync'd event replays intact from a fresh OpenJournal. Both layers must use the same Journal type and on-disk layout so their composition is sound.
decisions.rationale: validation.md section 2 requires real process signals, and only Layer B gives a real SIGKILL against real fsync durability. But a full-daemon end-to-end crash test is where flakiness lives, and flaky policy section 9 forbids promoting a variable result, so the state-machine claim must not depend on process timing. Layer B is deterministic on GitHub Actions ubuntu-latest because it needs no privilege, no namespace and no container: its only synchronisation is polling for a marker file the child writes strictly after fsync returns, with a bounded deadline and t.Fatal on timeout, never a fixed sleep. Layer A is deterministic because the clock is injected and every tick is an explicit call.

decisions.decision: Change the journal recovery key from the per-attempt request id to the stable increment/target identity plus an operation kind, and give the journey an explicit attempt number that derives per-attempt canonical request ids (RequestID:attempt-N:claim, and so on).
decisions.rationale: Orchestrator.pendingResult looks up id+":result_pending" where id is JourneyRequest.RequestID, and every canonical call reuses that same RequestID. A second attempt with the same RequestID therefore hits application idempotency and returns the original ClaimResponse, which is why TestOrchestratorFakeJourney proves same-Execution retry idempotence and cannot prove resume in a different Execution. A second attempt with a fresh RequestID gets a new Execution but loses the journal lookup. Resume across Executions needs the durable key to be the identity that survives the crash (the Increment) while the canonical fence stays per attempt.

decisions.decision: Wire the runner's provider boundary to the existing provider-neutral contract without modifying internal/provider at all. Delete the Prompt field from runner.ProviderRequest, carry provider.WorkPacket instead, and add a runner-side ProviderClient composed of a provider.Adapter (Build/Parse) and an InvocationRunner seam. Ship FakeInvocationRunner (returns fixture bytes, records the Invocation) for V2-016 and SupervisedInvocationRunner (real exec through ProcessSupervisor plus the bounded log) as the seam V2-017 fills with a real CLI. Tests build the Invocation with the real provider.CodexAdapter and parse a generated fixture with the real CodexAdapter.Parse, so the real argv and parse contract are exercised with zero quota consumption.
decisions.rationale: M3's stated outcome includes a provider-neutral Work Packet, and the completion condition that no credential reaches the Work Packet is unverifiable while the runner path has no Work Packet. Deleting Prompt makes a raw prompt structurally unrepresentable instead of merely asserted absent (the current test only checks Calls[0].Prompt == ""). Confining the change to internal/runner keeps V2-016 to a single evidence component: internal/provider's public API (WorkPacket, Adapter, Invocation, Result, ClassifyError, DigestOutput) is already sufficient, Invocation.Environment is already the injection point the Secret Broker needs, and internal/provider imports only the standard library so there is no cycle. docs/operations/v2-task-dag.md section 5 assigns the provider component's evidence to V2-027 (M6), so a change under internal/provider here would need a second evidence record owned by a different milestone.

decisions.decision: Implement a local Secret Broker in internal/runner with two structurally separate environment channels. The guarded base environment (GuardEnvironment allowlist, still rejecting secret-shaped names and values) is what the bounded log and the journal may observe. The granted channel is produced only by SecretBroker.Lease for one scope (execution id, repository, provider, fencing token, expiry) and one Invocation, is merged into the child environment inside the supervisor, and is never returned to any code path that writes the journal, the Work Packet, the canonical store or the log. Grants are revocable and single-use; Lease fails closed on expiry, on an effective stop (domain.PermitCredential denied), and on a credential name outside the per-provider allowlist. Only the credential identifier is ever recorded.
decisions.rationale: overview.md's Secret Broker requires scope-limited injection, no credential in Work Packet, canonical state or Artifact, and no new issuance after stop or expiry. The two-channel split resolves a real contradiction in the current code: GuardEnvironment rejects any secret-shaped variable name, so a broker that injected through the guarded environment would either be rejected or force the guard to be weakened. Keeping the channels separate lets the guard stay strict on everything the runner declares while the credential travels a path that is, by construction, not reachable from any serialiser.

decisions.decision: Add a bounded diagnostic log sink in internal/runner: per-execution 0600 file under the data root (not under the workspace, so the child cannot read or tamper with it), hard byte and line caps, an explicit truncation marker, and RedactLog applied to every write.
decisions.rationale: validation.md section 2 requires bounded log and redaction and overview.md requires a capacity-limited local diagnostic log, but today RedactLog is a bare function with no sink and no bound; only the journal is bounded. Without a sink there is nothing to point the redaction assertion at, so the non-leakage condition cannot be verified at runtime.

decisions.decision: Verify 'no credential in Control Plane, Work Packet or log' three ways, and require a positive control for each negative assertion. (1) Static: extend the V2-010 go/ast source-guard pattern to internal/runner's non-test files, proving no credential-shaped field exists on any type that is marshalled into a journal event, a Work Packet, a canonical application request or a log line, with the matcher itself verified against known-positive and known-negative names so it cannot pass vacuously. (2) Runtime: generate a credential fixture in the test (crypto/rand derived, secret-shaped, never a real credential), pass it through the broker, and assert the value's bytes appear in none of the journal file, the marshalled Work Packet, the bounded log file, the canonical store's recorded events, or the process argv, while asserting it does appear in Invocation.Environment so the search is proven non-vacuous. (3) Redaction: an unbrokered secret-shaped value emitted on child stdout must land in the log as [REDACTED], and a non-secret value must survive unchanged.
decisions.rationale: The static guard catches the schema-level regression that a runtime test cannot see (a field added but not yet populated); the runtime test catches the leak a static guard cannot see (a correctly typed field carrying the value into a serialiser). validation.md section 6 requires positive controls, and V2-010 already showed that a text grep for the word credential fails on legitimate code such as PermitCredential, which is why the static layer must read the AST rather than the file text. The non-goal that no real credential is used is satisfied because the fixture is generated in-process and never written outside t.TempDir().

decisions.decision: Add a runner-side lease keeper that calls application Renew and application Heartbeat as two separate operations, driven by an injected clock and explicit ticks, and exercise it in journey 1 with a provider run that spans more than one LeaseTTL.
decisions.rationale: The roadmap lists heartbeat and Lease among M3's outcomes and overview.md requires heartbeat and progress events to be separate, but the Orchestrator never renews: with LeaseTTL of one minute, any provider run longer than the TTL loses its lease mid-flight. Nothing in the repository currently exercises Renew or Heartbeat from the runner side. Explicit ticks over an injected clock keep the test deterministic; a background timer would make it timing-dependent.

decisions.decision: Strengthen the process-group test instead of adding a new one: spawn a child that spawns a grandchild in the same new process group, and assert that the grandchild is actually gone and that TERM was delivered before KILL, observed through files the children write, polled with a bounded deadline.
decisions.rationale: TestSupervisorCancelsProcessGroupTERMThenKILL currently asserts only that Run returns a non-nil error, which the bare context deadline already guarantees. It would still pass if syscall.Kill were removed entirely, so it does not verify the property validation.md section 2 asks for. This is a strengthening of an existing assertion, not a re-implementation.

decisions.decision: Scope workspace write confinement for M3 local to what the local closure can actually prove: that the runner never hands the child a path outside the workspace (Invocation.WorkingDirectory equals the resolved workspace, no argv element resolves outside it, the environment is allowlisted, and the workspace is not a symlink and not group or world accessible), plus a detection assertion that any write landing outside the workspace tree is caught. OS-enforced namespace confinement is explicitly out of scope for V2-016 and is escalated as a container or VM integration test.
decisions.rationale: technology.md section 10 specifies a namespace sandbox, but namespace confinement needs privileges that are not reliably available on GitHub Actions ubuntu-latest, so requiring it here would produce either a skipped test recorded as passing or an intermittent failure, both of which flaky policy section 9 forbids. Claiming OS enforcement while only asserting convention would be exactly the substitution G3 rejects, so the packet states the weaker property truthfully and names the stronger one as deferred.

decisions.decision: Keep the existing fsync-backed JSONL journal as the Runner local durable store. Do not introduce SQLite in V2-016. Record the substitution in docs/operations/runner-local.md and escalate the technology.md and validation.md wording to product_orchestrator.
decisions.rationale: technology.md section 10 and validation.md section 2 both name SQLite for the Runner local journal and cache, but adding it means a new third-party dependency and a go.mod or go.sum change, and evidenceKey() includes go.mod and go.sum in every component hash, so the whole evidence ledger would be invalidated for a storage-engine swap that changes no M3 completion condition. The properties the docs actually rely on (durable append, fsync, idempotent replay, partial-tail tolerance, corruption rejection, bounded size) are already implemented and tested. This is a doc-versus-implementation divergence that a Tech Lead may not silently resolve in either direction, so it is recorded and escalated.

decisions.decision: Out of scope for V2-016, with the owning task named: real Codex Preview capability (V2-017, M3 live); offline claim and Result rejection, graceful/immediate/emergency stop journeys, and lost/orphan reconciliation end to end (V2-019, M4); atomic binary update and rollback (already covered by internal/update, matured in V2-034, M8); multi-Runner concurrent claim as a journey (V2-030, M7); Claude and opencode adapter fixtures (V2-027, M6). The old Execution remaining non-Lost in canonical state after a crash without a reconciler pass is accepted here; only the safety-relevant half, rejection of its late Result, is asserted.
decisions.rationale: docs/operations/v2-task-dag.md section 5 states that validation.md section 2 is a test-pyramid target rather than a milestone gate checklist, and that requiring behaviour that does not yet exist produces declarations instead of verification. Lost and orphan reconciliation is literally M4's stated outcome, so pulling it into M3 would both duplicate V2-019 and force a cross-component import from internal/runner into internal/reconciler.

decisions.decision: Produce exactly one evidence record, .agents/v2/evidence/V2-016-runner.json, with id ev-v2-016-runner, task_id V2-016, component runner and result passed, registered in .agents/v2/evidence/index.json.
decisions.rationale: docs/operations/v2-task-dag.md section 5 assigns component runner to V2-016. The evidence id names the verification target and task_id names the producer, which is the convention that section 5 adopted after the active-evidence-task-identity-mismatch that failed V2-024. Confining all code changes to internal/runner and cmd/runner keeps a single component key in play, so one record is both necessary and sufficient.

decisions.decision: Do not correct ci/components.json in V2-016, and record the debt: the runner component declares dependencies [domain, update] while internal/runner already imports internal/application, and its tests already import internal/store/memory; V2-016 adds an import of internal/provider. The runner evidence key therefore does not invalidate when application, store-memory or provider change. Escalate the batched correction to product_orchestrator.
decisions.rationale: The gap pre-exists V2-016 and V2-016 adds one more instance of it rather than a new class of it. Fixing it means editing ci/components.json, which is in all_on_change and is hashed into every component key, so the correction should be batched into a single task at a milestone boundary where re-evidencing is already being paid, not paid twice. Note also that the depended-on components declare no public_contracts, so simply adding them to the dependency list would not change the key either: the fix is a design change to evidenceKey, which is a cross-boundary redesign and not this work order.

decisions.decision: On resume, the pre-crash local provider checkpoint recovered from the journal may be adopted by the new Execution, but the canonical AcceptResult must be submitted with the new Execution's own version and the new, strictly greater fencing token; the old Execution's Result must be rejected. Interpretation: safety invariant 11 forbids an expired token from advancing canonical state, and it does, because nothing is accepted under the old token; local provider output is Runner-local evidence, not a canonical Result.
decisions.rationale: Without this the resume case is unimplementable without re-running the provider, which for V2-017 means paying real quota for work already done. The interpretation is stated explicitly rather than assumed because invariant interpretation is a product_orchestrator decision: if Sol reads invariant 11 as forbidding adoption of any pre-fence work product, the resume path must instead always re-run the provider and this decision must be reversed before implementation.

verification: devbox run --pure -- go test -count=1 -v ./internal/runner (timeout 600s): the 11 pre-existing tests still pass unchanged in name and intent, plus the new journey, crash, secret broker, bounded log and source guard tests.
devbox run --pure -- go test -count=1 -race ./internal/runner ./cmd/runner (timeout 900s): the real-process crash test and the lease keeper are race-clean.
devbox run --pure -- make component-runner (timeout 600s): the runner component check target is green.
devbox run --pure -- go test -count=1 ./internal/contracts (timeout 300s): TestTaskPacketsValidate accepts both V2-016 packets and TestActiveEvidenceIndex accepts the registered evidence record.
devbox run --pure -- make check (timeout 2400s), run again after the evidence commit so that gitleaks git scans the committed history.
devbox run --pure -- make evidence-keys (timeout 600s) on the final formatted tree, to read the runner component evidence key that the record must carry.
risks: Deleting ProviderRequest.Prompt is a source-compatible break for orchestrator_test.go, which asserts Calls[0].Prompt is empty. That assertion must be replaced by the stronger structural claim (the field does not exist and a Work Packet is carried instead); leaving both would look like a re-implementation.

The real-process crash test is the one place flakiness could enter. It must synchronise only on a marker file written strictly after fsync returns, with a bounded deadline and t.Fatal on timeout. Any fixed sleep, or any dependence on scheduling order between the SIGKILL and the child's next write, must be rejected in review.

internal/application, internal/store/memory and internal/domain are prohibited here, so if the resume path turns out to need a canonical change (for example, a way to mark the crashed Execution lost without the reconciler), the task blocks rather than widening. That is intended, but it is the most likely stop point.

.agents/v2/evidence/index.json is being edited concurrently by two other implementers. The entry must be re-added after rebase and the evidence_hash recomputed on the final bytes; blindly resolving the conflict in favour of either side would drop another task's entry and fail TestActiveEvidenceIndex.

d17 rests on an interpretation of safety invariant 11. If product_orchestrator disagrees, the resume design changes shape (always re-run the provider) and the affected acceptance criteria must be rewritten before implementation rather than patched afterwards.

The runner evidence key will not invalidate when internal/application, internal/store/memory or internal/provider change (d16). Until that is fixed, a future change to those packages can leave the runner evidence stale while still being reported fresh, which is a freshness risk against validation.md section 8 rather than a correctness risk in this task.
